doc: The one source of truth for importing the player's saves from an installed original game (docs/WEB_PLAYER.md, 'Importing saves from an installed game'). The web listing page (web/saveimport.js, with this table as saveimport-table.js) and the native games (platform/SaveImport.cpp, with this table compiled in) both read it. Nothing outside this table is ever taken. A value or file pattern matches without regard to case; '*' stands for any characters inside one path part, '#' for digits. Registry value paths are relative to the game's key and use backslashes; file paths use slashes and are relative to the folder that holds the saves.

hives.vs: HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\Classes\VirtualStore\MACHINE\SOFTWARE\<WOW6432Node\><key>: where Windows redirects the writes of a game that was not run as administrator
hives.hklm: HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\<WOW6432Node\><key>: the 32-bit view that a 32-bit original uses

bookworm.note: The port follows the 2004 edition of the original Windows game (the one that keeps its players under the registry key Users). The Steam edition is a later build that keeps each player in players\<name>\profile.dat and scores.dat; the port does not read those.

bejeweledtwist.note: The Steam edition keeps its players in C:\ProgramData\Steam\BejeweledTwist (choose that folder) and its settings under HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\Steam\BejeweledTwist, which the import does not read: only the players and scores come over from it.

astropop.note: AstroPop keeps each player's file (users/data<n>.usr) in its game folder and a part of the player's settings in the registry under PopCap\AstroPop\Users; the game reads both, so both come over.

bejeweled2.note: The Steam edition keeps its players in C:\ProgramData\Steam\Bejeweled2 (choose that folder) and its settings under HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\Steam\Bejeweled2, the key this port reads too; a copy that keeps its settings elsewhere only brings its players and scores.

files.what: a player's games in progress, one for each mode

typershark.note: Typer Shark keeps the list of players and each player's file (users/user.idx, users/user<n>.dat) in its game folder and the rest of each player (the progress, the statistics, the settings) in the registry under PopCap\TyperShark\Users; the game reads both, so both come over.
